title: Spec of a quotient ring is homeomorphic to the zero locus
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq R$ an ideal and $q:R\to R/J$ the quotient map; more generally let $q:R\to S$ be a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel $J$. Then the map $\operatorname{Spec}q:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\bar{\mathfrak p}\mapsto q^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak p})$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], is injective, its image is the closed subset $V(J)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R: J\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$, and it is a homeomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ onto $V(J)$ with the subspace topology (a closed embedding); the inverse sends $\mathfrak p\in V(J)$ to $q(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Algebra, section "The spectrum of a ring", Lemma Tag 00E5 (lemma-spec-closed), algebra.tex:3227-3235
